title: No, local models will not win
gist: Argues datacenter inference is cheaper for structural reasons, not subsidy: batching serves many users for about the cost of one, a single local user has nothing to batch, and datacenter chips do more per watt. Users also choose the strongest model they can get.
changes: The cleanest statement of why the loop's home is the datacenter. Every agent-loop result tracked here leans on batching and cache reuse across many sessions, which one user does not have.
caveats: The 30x figure is a back-of-envelope product of the author's own estimates. It ignores speculation, several local agents sharing a batch, and privacy. He concedes a hybrid (local for fast, cloud for hard) is likely.

numbers.metric: Resources per unit of inference, local against datacenter
numbers.baseline: the author's estimate from chip specifications and batching

bears_on.note: The economics that make the datacenter loop pay (batching, shared caches) are absent for one user.

retired_why: Out of scope. On 19 Nov the reader clarified that local means fitted to what you have (different devices), not on-device hardware, so the on-device question is no longer tracked.
